subject.title: [Feature]: `openclaw backup`: support manifest-backed intentional omissions for protected or reconstructable runtime paths

question: Should core backup support operator-declared omissions, and if so should one versioned omission-plan file become the sole supported input and manifest contract?
rationale: The input location, path anchoring, wildcard expansion, classification vocabulary, manifest compatibility, and verification rules define the security meaning of a successful backup.

options.title: Adopt one versioned plan
options.body: Add an explicit plan-file CLI input whose rules resolve to concrete manifest omissions and whose unmatched or undeclared failures remain fatal.

options.title: Allow built-in classes only
options.body: Expand only core-maintained volatile and reconstructable path classifications without accepting arbitrary operator-defined omissions.

options.title: Retain strict inclusion
options.body: Keep the present behavior and require protected datasets to be relocated, made readable, or backed up by a separate producer.

recommendation.title: Adopt one versioned plan
recommendation.body: Add an explicit plan-file CLI input whose rules resolve to concrete manifest omissions and whose unmatched or undeclared failures remain fatal.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and performed substantial hardening of the existing backup planner, manifest, verifier, and path-safety boundaries.
